title: LLVM / Clang
description: LLVM with any of its sub-projects (clang, lld, lldb, flang, ...) plus the runtimes (libc++, compiler-rt, ...).

stages.title: Base packages
stages.description: cmake, ninja, host gcc and clang, and every library the projects can use. Only changes with the Ubuntu version.

stages.title: LLVM + projects
stages.description: cmake + ninja install of LLVM, clang, lld, ...

stages.title: Runtimes
stages.description: libc++, libc++abi, libunwind, compiler-rt, ... built by the new clang in a separate standalone build.

options.label: Projects
options.description: Sub-projects built together with LLVM (LLVM_ENABLE_PROJECTS). Dependencies are selected automatically.

choices.label: clang
choices.description: The C/C++/Objective-C compiler. Needed for the runtimes.

choices.label: lldb
choices.description: The LLVM debugger, with Python scripting.

choices.label: flang
choices.description: The Fortran compiler. Very memory hungry to build. From LLVM 21 it needs the flang-rt runtime.

options.label: Targets
options.description: Code generators to build (LLVM_TARGETS_TO_BUILD). 'host' is the architecture Docker builds on. Fewer targets build faster.

choices.label: host
choices.description: Whatever architecture the build machine is.

options.label: Experimental targets
options.description: LLVM_EXPERIMENTAL_TARGETS_TO_BUILD.

sections.title: LLVM build
sections.description: How LLVM and the projects are compiled.

options.label: Host compiler
options.description: Which Ubuntu compiler builds LLVM. Both are installed in the base layer.

choices.label: clang (Ubuntu package)
choices.description: Needed for ThinLTO/full LTO builds of LLVM.

options.label: Build type
options.description: CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE for LLVM and the projects.

choices.label: RelWithDebInfo
choices.description: -O2 -g. Large, and linking needs a lot of memory.

choices.label: Debug
choices.description: Unoptimised with debug info. Very large and slow.

options.label: Linker used to build
options.description: LLVM_USE_LINKER. lld and mold are much faster than GNU ld for LLVM's large binaries.

options.label: LTO of LLVM itself
options.description: LLVM_ENABLE_LTO. Faster compiler, much slower build. Needs host compiler clang and linker lld.

options.label: Assertions
options.description: LLVM_ENABLE_ASSERTIONS. Useful when developing against LLVM; slows the compiler by 10-20%.

options.label: Shared libLLVM
options.description: Build libLLVM.so and link the tools against it, as distributions do. Much smaller install.

options.label: Shared libclang-cpp
options.description: Link the clang tools against libclang-cpp.so. Needs Shared libLLVM.

options.label: RTTI
options.description: LLVM_ENABLE_RTTI. Needed by some out-of-tree users of the LLVM libraries.

options.label: Exceptions
options.description: LLVM_ENABLE_EH. Needs RTTI.

options.label: zstd compression
options.description: Compressed debug sections, profile data, ...

options.label: zlib compression
options.description: zlib support.

options.label: libxml2
options.description: Used by lld's COFF manifests and lldb.

options.label: LLVMgold linker plugin
options.description: Build LLVMgold.so so GNU ld (with -plugin) can link clang -flto objects. Uses Ubuntu's binutils-dev headers.

options.label: Toolchain only
options.description: Install only the compilers, linkers and tools, without the LLVM/clang libraries and headers needed to build against LLVM. Makes the image several GB smaller.

options.label: Install test utilities
options.description: Install FileCheck, not, count, ... (handy for lit tests of out-of-tree projects).

options.label: Optimised tablegen
options.description: Build tablegen in release mode even for Debug builds. Speeds up debug builds.

options.label: Parallel link jobs
options.description: Limit concurrent links to save memory (for example 4 for Debug or LTO builds). Empty means no limit.

options.label: Default target triple
options.description: Empty uses the host triple.

options.label: Extra C flags
options.description: CMAKE_C_FLAGS for the LLVM build, for example -march=x86-64-v3.

options.label: Extra C++ flags
options.description: CMAKE_CXX_FLAGS for the LLVM build.

options.label: Extra CMake arguments
options.description: Appended to the LLVM cmake command as written (shell syntax).

options.label: Strip installed binaries
options.description: ninja install/strip removes debug symbols from the installed programs and runtimes.

sections.title: Clang defaults
sections.description: What the installed clang uses when no flag says otherwise.

options.label: Default C++ library
options.description: CLANG_DEFAULT_CXX_STDLIB (what -stdlib= defaults to).

options.label: Default runtime library
options.description: CLANG_DEFAULT_RTLIB (what --rtlib= defaults to).

options.label: Default unwinder
options.description: CLANG_DEFAULT_UNWINDLIB (what --unwindlib= defaults to).

options.label: Default linker
options.description: CLANG_DEFAULT_LINKER (what -fuse-ld= defaults to).

options.label: PIE by default
options.description: CLANG_DEFAULT_PIE_ON_LINUX.

sections.title: Runtimes
sections.description: Standard library and compiler runtime, built in their own layer by the new clang.

options.label: Runtimes
options.description: LLVM_ENABLE_RUNTIMES for a standalone runtimes build. Changing anything in this section does not rebuild the compiler.

choices.label: libc++abi
choices.description: C++ ABI library (exceptions, RTTI) under libc++.

choices.label: flang-rt
choices.description: The Fortran runtime (needs the flang project).

options.label: Build type
options.description: CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE for the runtimes.

options.label: libc++ hardening mode
options.description: Default _LIBCPP_HARDENING_MODE for code built against this libc++.

choices.label: extensive
choices.description: Most checks that do not change complexity.

options.label: libc++ ABI version
options.description: Version 2 is the unstable ABI with layout improvements; binaries are incompatible with version 1.

options.label: Exceptions in libc++
options.description: Turn off to build a -fno-exceptions libc++ / libc++abi.

options.label: Merge libc++abi into libc++.a
options.description: LIBCXX_ENABLE_STATIC_ABI_LIBRARY: static linking needs only -lc++.

options.label: libc++abi uses libunwind
options.description: LIBCXXABI_USE_LLVM_UNWINDER. Off uses libgcc_s for unwinding.

options.label: Runtimes use compiler-rt
options.description: Link libc++, libc++abi and libunwind against compiler-rt builtins instead of libgcc (a GCC-free C++ stack).

options.label: compiler-rt: sanitizers
options.description: ASan, UBSan, TSan, MSan, ... (the bulk of compiler-rt's build time).

options.label: compiler-rt: XRay
options.description: Function call tracing.

options.label: compiler-rt: libFuzzer
options.description: -fsanitize=fuzzer.

options.label: compiler-rt: profile
options.description: PGO and coverage (-fprofile-instr-generate).

options.label: compiler-rt: memprof
options.description: Heap profiler.

options.label: compiler-rt: ORC
options.description: ORC JIT runtime.

options.label: compiler-rt: host target only
options.description: Skip the i386 variants on x86_64 hosts.

options.label: Extra C flags
options.description: CMAKE_C_FLAGS for the runtimes.

options.label: Extra C++ flags
options.description: CMAKE_CXX_FLAGS for the runtimes.

options.label: Extra CMake arguments
options.description: Appended to the runtimes cmake command as written (shell syntax).

rules.message: LTO builds of LLVM are best linked with lld.
The clang project is not selected, so the Clang defaults and the runtimes are skipped.
clang defaults to libc++ but the libcxx runtime is not selected.
clang defaults to compiler-rt but the compiler-rt runtime is not selected.
clang defaults to libunwind but the libunwind runtime is not selected.
clang defaults to lld but the lld project is not selected.
'Runtimes use compiler-rt' needs the compiler-rt runtime.
libc++abi is set to use libunwind but the libunwind runtime is not selected.
From LLVM 21 flang needs the flang-rt runtime to link Fortran programs.
flang needs roughly 4-6 GB of memory per compile job. Consider limiting parallel link jobs.
